contexts.text: I am thy shield () = protection against evils and falsities, which is trusted. AC 1788, Illustrated.

Shield, relatively to the Lord, = protection against evils and falsities; relatively to man, = confidence in the Lord; because it was a protection for the breast, and the breast = good and truth. Illustrated.
Shield, in the opposite, = the evils and falsities from which they fight, which defend them, and in which they confide. Illustrated.
Buckler, shield, etc. = all things of doctrine.
His Truth a shield and buckler () = a guard by truth.
Thou wilt encompass them as with a shield () = His protection from love.
(Signification of a shield as distinguished from that of a buckler. See Buckler.)
